Thanks for taking our initial call last week. As discussed, Halcyon is compiling a short list of inference vendors for our pilot: Redwood, NimbusAI, and one other. Procurement asked us to collect a compact commercial comparison and any flexibility on first-year pricing and onboarding credits.

Can you send a one-page commercial summary plus rough TCO assumptions (hosted vs. dedicated) and any standard swap incentives you typically offer to match competitor pricing? We have an internal deadline of Feb 1 to finalize the pilot vendor.

Attached is our RFP excerpt and a quick list of expected call volume/peak QPS.

Thanks,

Hi Marta —

Appreciate the RFP excerpt. I've attached a one-page commercial summary and a simple TCO workbook that maps hosted vs dedicated cost for your projected volumes. Highlights up front:
- Pilot credit: $25k onboarding credit (applies to hosted API pilot).
- Price match policy: we can consider aligning with a verified public commercial offer for the first 12 months up to a capped concession; details below.
- Dedicated option: 10–15% unit-cost reduction at predictable throughput; onboarding timeline ~6–8 weeks.

I'll summarize the key delta versus NimbusAI in the doc, including runtime compatibility and how our caching/batching lowers per-token cost for your QPS profile. If you want, Karthik and I can run a 30-minute runbook session with Samir and your procurement team next week.

Thanks Priya — initial materials look useful. Procurement (copied Samir) has asked for a concrete counter: NimbusAI has offered a 40% list discount across tokens for year one plus 3 months free onboarding credits and a reduced minimum MRR for the first 6 months. They also provided a redlineable term sheet.

Can Redwood match that for year one (we're primarily evaluating economics for a 12-month pilot-to-commit path)? If not, what is the maximum allowable concession and what conditionalities would apply (commitment length, seat counts, SLA holdbacks)?

Also: is there a mechanism to escrow performance (e.g., performance credits tied to latency SLOs) — procurement wants low risk if we switch.

Marta

On a separate note, Samir — if Redwood can come close on price it's likely the technical team will favor them on deployment flexibility.

Fwding Marta's counter. Quick context: they want a straight year-one price-match (40% off list) + 3 months onboarding credits. Procurement explicitly asked for an escrow/performance-credit mechanism.

Quote from Marta's email below:
> NimbusAI has offered a 40% list discount across tokens for year one plus 3 months free onboarding credits and a reduced minimum MRR for the first 6 months.

Questions for ops/commercial:
1) Maximum concession we can approve without CS/RevOps signoff? (Jonas)
2) If we offer a 30% first-year discount + $25k onboarding credits, what is the expected impact on unit economics for their projected QPS in pricing_breakdown.xlsx? Any ability to move to deeper discount if they commit to a dedicated pool? (Karthik)
3) Escrow/performance-credit: we can offer SLA-based credits (standard) and an implementation warranty; fine to structure as a holdback paid if SLOs not met for first 90 days. Is that acceptable legal-wise?

Suggest we aim to keep the public list-to-net delta capped at 30% unless we secure a 12–18 month commit or a dedicated reserved capacity purchase. If we need to stretch, ask for an internal approval path (discount cap + required RevOps approval).

— Priya

Hi Marta / Samir —

Thanks for the clarity. We ran the numbers and can present a conditional match that aligns closely with NimbusAI while protecting both sides during the migration window. Summary of the counter-offer:

- Commercial: 30% off list token pricing for month 1–12.
- Onboarding: $30k onboarding credit (applies to implementation & pilot consumption).
- Commitment: 12-month term with a 9-month minimum usage commitment (true-up at month 12 based on committed volume).
- Dedicated option: if Halcyon converts to a Dedicated pool within 90 days, we will increase the year-one discount to 37% and provide a one-time migration credit of $50k toward dedicated ramp.
- SLA/escrow: we will include an implementation holdback of 5% of the first quarter value in escrow; performance credits will be tripped against latency SLOs (detailed SLA schedule attached). Holdback is returned pro rata if SLOs are met.
- Legal/Docs: I'll send a redlineable term sheet via DocuSign for procurement review (link below).

Conditions and why: the 30% baseline keeps unit economics within acceptable thresholds for hosted pilots at their projected QPS (see pricing_breakdown.xlsx). The dedicated incentive requires a committed convert to avoid cannibalizing hosted margins. The holdback protects Halcyon during cutover and is a standard mitigation we can sign off on with Legal.

Next steps: if that looks acceptable I'll generate a term sheet and schedule a 30-minute commercial call with Samir and technical ops to lock down migration milestones.
